newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FDP says Eurofighter unaffordable.
newsitem.headline: German FDP says Eurofighter unaffordable.

text.p: The German government cannot afford to buy the Eurofighter plane being jointly developed by Germany, Britain, Spain and Italy, said Juergen Koppelin, budget expert of the Free Democrats.
"In the current budget situation it is completely impossible," Koppelin, whose party is the junior partner in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, said on Tuesday.

Under pressure to rein in the budget deficit this year so Germany will qualify for European monetary union, Finance Minister Theo Waigel is expected to ask all government ministries for greater cost-cutting efforts.

Koppelin said before the final decision is made on whether to order the planes, the government must consider whether production could be postponed, or whether industry could provide the upfront financing, the model used to produce submarines.
The decision whether to order the planes is expected to be made by mid-summer, when Waigel draws up the budget for 1988.

Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, who wants Bonn to buy 180 Eurofighters for 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion), has said he can no longer exclude a German withdrawal from the project because of the budget problems.
Ruehe, in an interview published on Tuesday in the Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung, said there was no further room for savings in the stretched defence budget.
Koppelin said Daimler-Benz Aerospace, the German partner in the project, was wrong to argue that many jobs depend on the Eurofighter.
If Bonn goes ahead with a Eurofighter it cannot afford, that would jeopardise investments in other areas such as shipbuilding and tanks that also create jobs, he said.
DASA's partners in the Eurofighter consortium are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.
